hero.heading:
Starting small.
Building boldly.
hero.body: NEXUS Robotics Kids Academy is a new learning space for curious kids who want to build, code, and understand how technology works.

story.heading: A new kind of after-school learning
paragraphs: We are building NEXUS around a simple idea: children learn technology best by making with it. A robot that moves, a circuit that lights up, or a small website that works can turn an abstract concept into a real moment of discovery.

As a new business, we are starting with a focused set of programmes and a close relationship with families. That gives us room to listen, improve the details, and shape each learning experience around the children in front of us.

Our first tracks bring together robotics, coding, electronics, web design, and AI for ages 6–16. Every learner gets a clear starting point, practical projects, and encouragement to keep experimenting.

mission.text: To make hands-on robotics and coding education accessible to every curious child — building technical skills, creative confidence, and the habit of learning by doing.

vision.text: A growing community of young builders who do more than use technology — they understand it, question it, and create with it.

pillars.heading: Hands-on first
pillars.body: Every concept is introduced through building. Theory follows practice, never the other way around.

pillars.heading: Fail fast
pillars.body: Mistakes are data. We encourage iteration and celebrate the moments when things don't work the first time.

pillars.heading: Ask why
pillars.body: Before we ask how to build something, we ask whether it should be built — and who it serves.

pillars.heading: Team over individual
pillars.body: Robotics is a team sport. Communication and collaboration are core skills — not extras.

team.heading: Meet the team
team.body: Our team brings together patient coaching, technical curiosity, and a belief that every child can make meaningful progress with the right project and support.

members.name: Alex Chen
members.bio: Leads beginner robotics sessions with clear builds, patient coaching, and plenty of time for kids to test their ideas.

members.name: Priya Nair
members.bio: Helps learners turn open-ended challenges into manageable steps, from the first sketch to a working robot.
members.imageAlt: Priya Nair, Robotics and Challenge Coach

members.name: Jordan Park
members.bio: Makes electronics, coding, and AI approachable through small experiments with visible, satisfying results.

members.name: Sam Torres
members.bio: Guides web projects and custom builds, helping students move from a digital idea to a physical prototype.
members.imageAlt: Sam Torres, Web Dev & 3D Printing Lead

timeline.heading: Building the programme from the ground up

events.title: Opening our first cohorts
events.body: We are welcoming our first learners into a focused set of robotics, coding, electronics, web, and AI programmes.

events.title: Improving through feedback
events.body: We listen to students and families, then refine projects, pacing, and support so each cohort gets a better experience.

events.title: Growing the project library
events.body: New builds, experiments, and pathways will give learners more ways to explore technology at their own pace.

events.title: A community of young builders
events.body: As more families join us, we will create more opportunities for learners to share projects, collaborate, and keep building together.
